VeilRec Privacy Policy

Last updated: October 4, 2026

1. Introduction

This policy explains how VeilRec handles information when you use its photo, video, audio, media-management and purchase features. VeilRec is developed and operated by Mustafa Öner.

Features vary by platform. The protected Vault, scheduling, background-capture controls and sharing/export flows described below are currently implemented on Android. This policy does not imply that those features are available on iOS.

2. Information VeilRec accesses

VeilRec accesses the camera and microphone when you use recording features and grant the relevant permissions. It processes the resulting recordings and local information needed to manage them, such as media type, filenames, capture times, sizes and favorites.

Capture settings, schedule definitions, permission-request history and privacy acknowledgements are stored locally to support your choices and app operation. Purchase-related information is handled separately as described below. VeilRec does not provide an in-app account-registration flow.

3. Photos, videos and audio recordings

PHOTO creates photos, VIDEO creates videos, and AUDIO creates audio recordings. Android VIDEO can include microphone sound; the current iOS VIDEO implementation does not enable sound recording.

VeilRec processes captured media locally for saving, viewing, playback and previews. It does not include an automatic media-upload feature or send your recordings, thumbnails or Vault content to RevenueCat for billing. Operating-system backups and transfers, and copies you choose to share or export, are separate from this app behavior.

4. Local storage and Vault

Saved Library media is kept in VeilRec-managed private app storage. Ordinary Library files do not have the Vault's additional encryption and authentication protection.

On Android, media moved into Private Vault is encrypted in protected local storage. Viewing requires device authentication. Lock conceals private content and invalidates access; background and device-lock protections also restrict access. Restoring a Vault item creates an ordinary private Library copy outside Vault protection.

Vault media is not provided to the billing service. Moving media into Vault does not recall copies previously shared, exported or included in backups.

5. Permissions and your choices

  • Camera: used to take photos and record videos you choose to capture.
  • Microphone: used for audio recordings and Android video sound you choose to capture.
  • Android notifications: used for pending or active capture status, cancellation controls and scheduled reminders. On Android versions requiring notification permission, denying it prevents new background capture through the current app flow and can prevent reminders.
  • Android device authentication: used to authorize Vault access.

You can review permissions in device settings. Denying a permission can make its related feature unavailable. VeilRec's internal Library is not Apple Photos; the current iOS implementation does not request access to your Photos library.

6. Scheduled and background capture

On Android, you can configure capture delays, background operations and schedule reminders. A capture you start may continue while the app is not visible, using foreground services, ongoing notifications and the platform's camera/microphone indicators. VeilRec does not hide these indicators.

Schedule reminders invite you to open VeilRec. A reminder alone does not start the camera or microphone. Schedule definitions and reminder state are stored locally. Deleting a schedule cancels its associated future reminder and opening authorization; it does not delete saved recordings or stop a capture already running.

Reminder delivery and continued operation depend on permissions, power management and other platform restrictions. Exact execution times and automatic restoration after a device restart are not guaranteed.

7. Purchases and RevenueCat

Where billing is enabled, Google Play or the Apple App Store processes purchases. VeilRec uses RevenueCat to verify purchases and manage Pro access, including restoring purchases. VeilRec does not receive or process your payment-card details.

Billing may communicate with RevenueCat and the store when the app starts or resumes, as well as during purchase and restore requests. This can occur even if you have not purchased Pro. RevenueCat uses a generated app-specific identifier and purchase/entitlement information. It may also process transaction-verification data and basic device or app technical information needed to provide its service. A generated identifier is not a promise of complete anonymity.

VeilRec does not supply recording content or media metadata to billing. The current integration does not set customer name/email attributes or enable automatic advertising-identifier collection or SDK diagnostics. RevenueCat and the stores apply their own privacy practices to their processing.

8. Analytics and third-party processing

VeilRec does not integrate a separate general-purpose behavioral analytics or advertising SDK. RevenueCat provides purchase/subscription analytics and technical purchase-management services; this is different from tracking your capture or media-viewing activity through a general analytics feature.

The third-party services involved in enabled purchases are RevenueCat and the relevant app store. Their policies provide further details about their processing and retention:

  • RevenueCat Privacy Policy
  • Google Privacy Policy
  • Apple Privacy Policy

Third-party destinations you choose when sharing media have their own practices. VeilRec does not control what a receiving app or recipient does with its copy.

9. Retention and deletion

Saved local recordings remain until you delete them or app/device storage is removed, subject to storage availability and platform behavior. VeilRec does not apply a fixed automatic expiry period to saved Library media. Schedules and local preferences remain until changed, removed or handled by the app's existing operation.

Library and Vault deletion remove the selected saved items from VeilRec-managed storage. Temporary files and local recovery records can have different lifetimes; deleting an item is not a guarantee that every device-level trace or existing backup is erased. Temporary sharing copies can remain in app cache until cleanup or operating-system removal.

Deleting local media does not delete store or RevenueCat purchase records, cancel a subscription, or remove copies held by recipients or Gallery. Billing providers retain information under their applicable policies and obligations. For questions about billing-related privacy requests, contact the publisher using the contact details below; subscription management remains with your app store.

10. Sharing and exporting media

On Android, Share prepares a temporary read-only copy and opens the system share chooser. The app or destination you choose may retain or transmit that copy. Opening the chooser alone does not prove that a recipient received it.

Save to Gallery creates a separate public media copy on supported Android versions. The private original remains unless you separately delete or move it. Shared and exported copies are outside Vault protection and are not removed when you delete the VeilRec original.

11. Uninstalling, backups and device transfers

A normal full uninstall removes the app's private local storage, including its Library and Android Vault. It does not remove exported Gallery files, copies held by other apps, or third-party purchase records. Offloading an iOS app is different from deleting it and can preserve its documents.

Android cloud backup is disabled for VeilRec, and Vault uses storage excluded from Android automatic backup. Device-to-device transfer behavior can differ between Android manufacturers, so this is not a promise that all app data is excluded from every transfer.

On iOS, Library media is stored in the app's Documents area and may be included in iCloud or computer backups according to your settings and platform behavior. No app-specific backup exclusion has been established for these files. VeilRec deletion does not remove pre-existing operating-system backups; manage those through the platform's backup controls.

12. Security

VeilRec uses app-private storage, platform permission controls and additional encryption/authentication for Android Vault content. RevenueCat documents encrypted transport for billing communications. No app or storage system can guarantee absolute security, and ordinary Library, shared and exported copies do not inherit Vault protection.

Protect your device and its authentication credentials. Only record people or places when you have permission or another legal right to do so.

13. Children and age considerations

VeilRec does not include child-specific features or an in-app age-verification flow. Use of recording features must respect other people's privacy and applicable recording rules. A parent or guardian should review a child's use of device recording permissions and store purchases. Store age ratings and purchase controls apply separately.

14. Changes to this policy

The publisher may update this policy when app behavior, providers or applicable requirements change. The latest version will carry a revised last-updated date. Review it when you update the app or use new features.

15. Contact

Publisher / Operator: Mustafa Öner

For questions about privacy, data practices or support, and deletion/privacy-related requests where applicable, contact veilrec.support@gmail.com.

Do not send device PINs, passwords, payment-card details or private recordings unless they are necessary for a request and you intentionally choose to share them. VeilRec's local recordings are not held in a developer-operated media cloud.

No tracking scripts, cookies or remote fonts are included on this page. The hosting provider may process web requests under its own privacy practices.
